mcat_description.short: Polyhouse Construction Services covers end-to-end turnkey construction of polyethylene-covered protected cultivation structures — including GI pipe framework fabrication, UV-stabilised poly film installation, ventilation systems, and optional drip irrigation — supplied as a complete project service to farmers and agri-entrepreneurs.
mcat_description.long: Polyhouse Construction Services in India encompasses the design, supply of materials, fabrication, and on-site installation of protected cultivation structures (polyhouses/greenhouses) using hot-dip galvanised iron pipe frameworks and UV-stabilised polyethylene film cladding, built to NHB/MIDH government specifications. The two dominant construction types are Naturally Ventilated Polyhouses (NVPH), which use passive top and side vents for air circulation, and Fan & Pad (high-tech) polyhouses, which use evaporative cooling for precise climate control. Service scope typically includes site preparation, structural erection, poly film fixing with aluminium/GI profiles and zig-zag springs, insect netting, side curtains, and integration of drip irrigation or fogging systems. Most projects in India are executed under NHB or NHM/MIDH government subsidy schemes, requiring the contractor to build to approved DPR specifications and pass a Joint Inspection Team (JIT) verification before subsidy release.

market_context: Polyhouse Construction Services in India is a fast-growing B2B agricultural infrastructure segment driven by government-backed protected cultivation promotion under the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), National Horticulture Board (NHB), and National Horticulture Mission (NHM) schemes. The two dominant construction types are Naturally Ventilated Polyhouses (NVPH) — the most widely built, cost-effective type suited to most Indian climates — and Fan & Pad (high-tech) polyhouses for precise climate control in hot/arid regions. Structural specifications are standardised under NHB/MIDH guidelines: GI pipes must be hot-dip galvanised as per IS 1161 and IS 4759:2019 with 275 GSM zinc coating; cladding is 200-micron UV-stabilised 3-layer PE film; welding is not permitted in main structural members. Government subsidy of up to 50% (general category) and up to 85–95% (SC/ST, state top-up) is available as a credit-linked back-ended grant under NHB/NHM/MIDH, making subsidy eligibility a critical purchase driver — buyers actively seek contractors who are empanelled with state horticulture departments and can assist with DPR preparation and JIT inspection compliance. Typical project sizes range from 500 sq m (small NHM projects) to 4,000 sq m per beneficiary under NHM, and larger under NHB. High-value crops grown include coloured capsicum, tomato, cucumber, rose, gerbera, and strawberry. States with high polyhouse adoption include Maharashtra, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Gujarat, and Rajasthan.
